randomized_air_hockey.notes: Paper-reported >98% online success after about 1300 of 2000 trials, with 1020 silicon neurons. These numbers are retained for provenance and are not scored targets on the local software scale.

velocity_range_wide.notes: Paper-reported approximately 93% asymptotic online success on [0.7, 1.5] m/s, versus 97% on [0.7, 0.9] m/s. These numbers are retained for provenance and are not scored targets on the local software scale.

velocity_range_extreme.notes: Paper-reported 86% online success on [0.5, 2.0] m/s, attributed to finite encoding resolution. These numbers are retained for provenance and are not scored targets on the local software scale.

_setup_note: Paper-reported numbers above are unchanged. The local software robot uses Eq. 1 for 64000 trials per chip (paper: 2000), 10 fixed chip instances, and final softmax-sampled held-out rollouts. Noise robustness uses 1020 units, 0.035 m position noise, 0.35 m/s velocity noise and 40 ms latency. Local reference results below were recomputed from isolated rollouts after all training and calibration completed.

velocity_range_extreme.description: Interception across the full 0.5–2.0 m/s speed range.
velocity_range_extreme.notes: Local software robot and spiking substrate, not silicon measurements. Ten fixed chips, 4096 paired episodes each with common observation noise and common action-sampling draws. Reference: 64000 trials; learning procedures are open. Coefficient zero means diagnostic only.

success_rate.description: Fraction of paired held-out episodes that reach x > 1.5 m with forward speed > 0.1 m/s, averaged over ten fixed chip instances.

seed_worst_success.description: Lowest success across the ten fixed chip instances; diagnostic reliability measure.

hit_rate.description: Fraction of episodes with physical puck–mallet contact; diagnostic, not a substitute for task success.

controller_units.description: Counted hidden units; must equal the assigned 1020-unit fixed instance. A violation fails every experiment.

single_core_extreme.description: Interception across 0.5–2.0 m/s with a single 256-unit instance.
